verses.text: Rehoboam went to Shechem; for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it (for he was in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of king Solomon), Jeroboam returned out of Egypt.
They sent and called him; and Jeroboam and all Israel came, and they spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
“Your father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make the grievous service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.”
He said to them, “Come again to me after three days.” So the people departed.
King Rehoboam took counsel with the old men, who had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, “What counsel do you give me about how to answer these people?”
They spoke to him, saying, “If you are kind to these people, please them, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever.”
But he abandoned the counsel of the old men which they had given him, and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
He said to them, “What counsel do you give, that we may give an answer to these people, who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Make the yoke that your father put on us lighter?’”

The young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, “Thus you shall tell the people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but make it lighter on us;’ thus you shall say to them, ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.
Now whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.’”
So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king asked, saying, “Come to me again the third day.”
The king answered them roughly; and king Rehoboam abandoned the counsel of the old men,
and spoke to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it. My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.”
So the king didn’t listen to the people; for it was brought about by God, that Yahweh might establish his word, which he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

When all Israel saw that the king didn’t listen to them, the people answered the king, saying, “What portion have we in David? We don’t have an inheritance in the son of Jesse! Every man to your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David.” So all Israel departed to their tents.
But as for the children of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.

Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was over the men subject to forced labor; and the children of Israel stoned him to death with stones. King Rehoboam hurried to get himself up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel rebelled against David’s house to this day.

footnotes.content: Rehoboam traveled to Shechem—the very place where Jacob once wrestled with God. He came to be crowned by all Israel, not knowing that the crown he grasped would slip through his fingers by day's end. Sometimes our greatest moments come just before our deepest tests.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeroboam heard and returned from Egypt—a man who once fled a king's wrath now drawn back by word of succession. How often the Lord uses old wounds and old wrongs to shape what comes next, though the man returns still bleeding.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They sent and called him—Jeroboam joined them to speak their grievance. One man's bitter memory of exile became a thousand voices crying for relief. The Lord knew what He was allowing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their plea was honest: Your father's yoke was grievous. They weren't asking to be lazy—they asked only for the weight to lighten. Sometimes a whole nation carries the burden of one man's reign, and they cry out not in rebellion but in raw need.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Come again after three days—Rehoboam asked for time to think, which was wise. Those three days held his future in them, though he didn't know it. Sometimes the Lord gives us a pause, hoping we'll use it to listen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He took counsel with the old men—Solomon's counselors, men who had seen kingdoms rise and fall. How merciful God was to place such wisdom within reach. Rehoboam had only to reach for it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you are kind to these people—the old men offered not flattery but truth. Kindness and good words open a door to loyalty that force never can. These elders knew the secret that many kings never learn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He abandoned the counsel of the old men—in one small choice, Rehoboam walked away from forty years of proven wisdom. His pride whispered that young blood knew better, and he listened. How the heart deceives us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What counsel do you give?—he asked his young companions, his friends, those who knew him not as king but as peer. We often seek out those who will tell us what we wish to hear, then call it wisdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My little finger is thicker than my father's waist—such arrogance dressed as humor. The young men spoke lies, and Rehoboam loved them for it. Pride finds listeners everywhere; it simply requires an audience hungry for the same disease.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will add to your yoke. I will chastise you with scorpions.—These words were not counsel; they were poison poured into a young man's ear. See how quickly cruelty replaces justice when pride is the only voice left to listen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They came the third day as the king asked—the people waited three days in hope, believing a new king might choose differently than his father. How patient they were, and how they were about to be broken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king answered them roughly—in that rough answer, Rehoboam sealed the fate of his own kingdom. One could almost feel the Spirit withdrawing, the Lord turning away to let the man learn by loss.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will add to it. I will chastise you with scorpions.—He spoke the poison aloud, as though saying it again would make it stronger. The people heard not their king but their enemy, and their hearts began to turn away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It was brought about by God, that Yahweh might establish his word—Here the chronicler reveals the hand beneath it all. What looked like Rehoboam's folly was the Lord fulfilling His word to Jeroboam. God works through our foolishness to accomplish His righteous purposes, though it costs us dearly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every man to your tents, Israel!—In that cry lies the rupture of a kingdom. The northern tribes turned their backs and went home to a life without the house of David. One foolish answer split what God had united, and the break would never fully mend.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But Rehoboam reigned over the children of Israel in the cities of Judah—he kept the south, but lost the north. Sometimes we count what remains and call it victory, not seeing the great thing we've lost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: King Rehoboam hurried to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem—he who came to be crowned fled in fear. His officers were stoned; he escaped with his life. The Lord had taught him a harsh lesson: pride runs, but it cannot outrun the cost of not listening.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this verse: how quickly we split what God has called whole—not always through grand rebellion, but through small refusals to listen to wisdom, through pride that dismisses the elders' counsel. The same spirit that divided a kingdom divides homes and communities still, and the cure remains the same: humble listening to those who have walked before us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
